results.title: The genus class number
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$ let $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ be the quadratic algebra $\mathbb Q[\omega]/(\omega^2+n)$. For $n\ge1$ the number $-n$ is not a square in $\mathbb Q$, so $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$ is a field, and a number field. For $n\ge1$ let $\mathrm{Cl}$ be the class group of the ring of integers of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-n})$. The *genus class number* of $n$ is the order of the subgroup of squares…

results.title: The statement of Rédei's formula
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: *Rédei's formula* is the following assertion. Let $d$ be odd and squarefree, and let $B$ be a nonempty set of primes of $d$ whose product $d_B=\prod_{p\in B}p$ satisfies $d_B\equiv7$, $3$ or $1\pmod8$. Then where $g(d_B)$ is the genus class number of $d_B$, the order of the subgroup of squares of the class group of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d_B})$, and $g_d(B)\in\mathbb F_2$ is Rédei's $g$ of $B$ for the bits $a_{pq}$,…

results.title: Rédei's formula
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Rédei's formula holds. Let $d$ be odd and squarefree, and let $B$ be a nonempty set of primes of $d$ with $d_B=\prod_{p\in B}p\equiv7$, $3$ or $1\pmod8$. Then the parity of the order of the subgroup of squares of the class group of $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-d_B})$ is Rédei's $g$ of $B$, computed from the residue bits of the primes of $d$.

results.title: The Rédei matrix
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $n$ be a natural number and $T_n$ its set of ramified primes: the primes of $n$, together with $2$ unless $n\equiv3\pmod4$. The *Rédei matrix* $R$ of $n$ is the matrix over $\mathbb F_2$ with rows indexed by the primes $q\mid n$ and columns by $T_n$, with entries where $[a/q]\in\mathbb F_2$ is the residue bit. A vector $e\in\mathbb F_2^{T_n}$ is *killed* by $R$ when $\sum_{p\in T_n}R_{qp}e_p=0$ for every prime…

results.title: The genus sum of class numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $d$ and a set $B$ of primes of $d$, the product $d_B=\prod_{p\in B}p$ is a positive integer, so its genus class number $g(d_B)$ is defined. The *genus sum of class numbers* of row 5b is the sum over the set partitions $\pi$ of the primes of $d$ with exactly one block $B$ having $d_B\equiv7\pmod8$, exactly one having $d_B\equiv3\pmod8$, and every block having $d_B\equiv7$, $3$ or $1\pmod8$.…

results.title: The certified rank hypothesis with class numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ_Cl is the following assertion. Let $d$ be squarefree with $d\equiv5\pmod8$. If $|\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)|=8$ and the genus sum of class numbers $T^{\rm Cl}_{5b}(d)$ is $1$, then for every $(a,b)\in\mathrm{Sel}_2(C_d)$ the 2-covering $D_{a,b}$ of $C_d$ has a rational point; that is, every 2-Selmer class of $C_d$ comes from a rational point.

results.title: The genus sum of class numbers is the genus sum of Rédei bits
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $d$ be odd and squarefree. Then the genus sum of row 5b with the genus class numbers $g(d_B)$ equals the genus sum with Rédei's $g_d(B)$. Along the way, the same identity is proved for every odd squarefree $d$ from Rédei's formula taken as an assumption.

results.title: CR₃ with class numbers is CR₃^TYZ
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The hypothesis CR₃^TYZ_Cl, stated with Tian, Yuan and Zhang's genus class numbers $g(d_B)$, holds if and only if the hypothesis CR₃^TYZ, stated with Rédei's $g_d(B)$, holds. Along the way, the same equivalence is proved from Rédei's formula taken as an assumption, and from the 4-rank statement taken as an assumption.
